text:
This section examines Iteration 20 —
Six-system SciML suite from

first principles. Keep two questions
separate: does changing the order

change the measured outcome, and does the
proposed search method

beat a matched alternative at the same
distinct-evaluation budget? Systems:

damped oscillator, cubic oscillator, Van
der Pol, Lotka–Volterra, Lorenz-63,

and Rössler. Six operations and all 720
orders per system,

4,320 rows total. Ordering effects
appeared in all six valid

system configurations; optima ranged from
one to eight per 720.

Insert was selected by rho_1 on all six,
suggesting general

precedence structure. Important
correction: Cayley/swap-aligned F D C

under-called search on Van der Pol,
Rössler, and Lotka–Volterra;

insert-prism dominated random despite
near-zero F D C. New lesson:

regime diagnosis should align its distance
metric with the detected

operator or combine strong
operator-specific rho_1 with F D C.

The distinction is part of the result. A
large ordering

effect does not automatically imply an
evolutionary-search advantage, and

almost-sure convergence does not promise
practical efficiency.
